labs.title: Build and verify a model-driven app for equipment requests
labs.summary: Use Power Apps to create a model-driven app from a Dataverse table, configure app pages, views, forms, sitemap navigation, a business rule, publish, and play the app to verify validation.
labs.scenario: Contoso Facilities needs a reliable internal app for equipment requests that coordinators can use without a custom canvas layout. In the simulated Power Apps maker portal, build a model-driven app, add the Equipment Request Dataverse table, choose the view and main form, configure navigation, add a form business rule, publish, and then play the app to prove validation works. Done means the runtime app opens and a high-priority request saves only when an estimated cost is provided.
learningObjectives: Explain why model-driven apps are suited to data-dense Dataverse processes
Add a Dataverse table page to a model-driven app
Choose table views and forms that shape the app experience
Configure sitemap navigation and a form business rule
Publish and play a model-driven app to verify behavior
prerequisites: Know that model-driven apps require Dataverse tables

steps.title: Create a model-driven app
steps.instruction: Go to **Apps**, select **+ New app**, choose **Model-driven app**, enter **Equipment Request Manager**, and select **Create**.
steps.hint: Choose model-driven for a data-dense process where Dataverse tables, views and forms drive the experience.
steps.explanation: Model-driven apps depend on a Dataverse data model and provide a consistent responsive interface.

rules.description: Equipment Request Manager model-driven app exists
rules.failureFeedback: Create the model-driven app named Equipment Request Manager.

steps.title: Add the Equipment Request table page
steps.instruction: In the app designer, select **Add page**, choose **Dataverse table**, select **Equipment Requests**, and select **Add**.
steps.hint: A Dataverse table page gives users list and record experiences based on table components.
steps.explanation: Adding a table page is the model-driven equivalent of adding a table-driven area to the app.

rules.failureFeedback: Add the Equipment Request Dataverse table to the app.

steps.title: Choose a view and form
steps.instruction: Select **Data experience**, choose view **Active Equipment Requests** and form **Main information**, then select **Save data experience**.
steps.hint: Views control record lists; forms control record details and editing.
steps.explanation: Model-driven apps compose Dataverse components instead of hand-placing every control.

rules.description: The app includes the required view and form
rules.failureFeedback: Add Active Equipment Requests and Main information to the app.

steps.title: Add form validation with a business rule
steps.instruction: Select **Business rules**, create **Require estimated cost for high priority**, set condition **Priority equals High**, action **Set Estimated cost as Business Required**, scope **Main information**, then **Save and activate**.
steps.hint: Business rules are no-code form logic. This rule prevents high-priority requests from being saved without a cost estimate.
steps.explanation: Business rules can enforce simple form behavior without JavaScript or plug-ins, which is important for maintainable low-code apps.

rules.description: The high-priority estimated cost rule is active
rules.failureFeedback: Activate the business rule that requires Estimated cost for high priority.

steps.title: Configure app navigation
steps.instruction: Select **Navigation**, set area **Requests**, add page **Equipment Requests**, and select **Save navigation**.
steps.hint: The sitemap controls the left navigation that users see at runtime.
steps.explanation: Navigation gives users a clear entry point to table pages and dashboards in a model-driven app.

rules.failureFeedback: Add Equipment Requests to the Requests area in navigation.

steps.title: Publish and verify the app
steps.instruction: Select **Save**, **Publish**, then **Play**. In the runtime app, select **New**, create a **High** priority request with an **Estimated cost**, and select **Save**.
steps.hint: Use a high-priority row with a cost estimate to prove the business rule permits valid data and would block missing cost.
steps.explanation: Publishing exposes the current designer metadata to users; playing the app validates the actual runtime experience.

rules.failureFeedback: Save and publish the model-driven app.

labs.solution:
1. Select **Apps** > **+ New app** > **Model-driven app**.
2. Enter `Equipment Request Manager` and select **Create**.
3. In the app designer, select **Add page** > **Dataverse table**, choose **Equipment Requests**, and select **Add**.
4. Select **Data experience**, choose view **Active Equipment Requests** and form **Main information**, then select **Save data experience**.
5. Select **Business rules**. Create `Require estimated cost for high priority` with condition **Priority equals High**, action **Set Estimated cost as Business Required**, scope **Main information**, then **Save and activate**.
6. Select **Navigation**, set area `Requests`, add page **Equipment Requests**, and select **Save navigation**.
7. Select **Save**, **Publish**, then **Play**.
8. In the runtime app, select **New**, create a high-priority request with an estimated cost, and select **Save**.
